title: Creating a Podcast Episode with AI: 200 years of digital technology milestones
html:
Creating a Podcast Episode with AI: 200 years of digital technology milestones

As a tech enthusiast, I recently decided to delve into researching the world of digital innovation in my personal capacity. Almost as soon as I began, I started coming across fascinating stories and milestones that have shaped this rapidly evolving landscape. So, I decided to capture them and over time, I have accumulated 48 (draft) pages of milestones and related stories. These milestones include, but are not limited to, data, data storage and collection, computing, major software development, standards, and advances in communication.

Recently, I stumbled upon Google’s NotebookLLM, an AI model with a remarkable ability to generate audio output. Intrigued by its potential, I decided to experiment with my research material. The results were nothing short of astonishing. The audio generated was impressively coherent and informative, capturing the essence of my research. It was clear that AI could be a valuable tool for transforming written content into engaging audio experiences.

Given the success of this initial experiment, I have decided to share the resulting podcast-like episode. By doing so, I hope to inspire others to explore the wonderful history of digital innovation and the creative possibilities of AI.

Embedded video: watch on YouTube

Andrej

Details / Disclaimers:

  1. PDF of my milestones
  2. Podcast created with Google’s NotebookLLM
  3. Image/thumbnail created with Google Gemini. Prompt: Create an image of a panel from a 1950s sci-fi comic where a non-gendered person is reflecting in the past 200 years of digital technology advancements. Ensure to include a webcam pointing at a coffee machine, a bar code drawn and a mobile phone from the early 1980s.
teaser: An experiment turning 48 draft pages of digital technology milestones into an AI-generated podcast episode with Google NotebookLM.
seo_description: Andrej Verity uses Google's NotebookLM to turn his research on 200 years of digital technology milestones into a podcast episode.
